subject: Service credit framework and temporary availability carve-out — BrightLoop
messages:
From: Jake Turner <jake.turner@brightloop.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Yoon <sara.yoon@brightloop.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Jul 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary uptime floor adjustment + monthly remedy proposal

Markus — thanks again for the product demo last week. BrightLoop's ops team did a quick run of our peak profile and we have a few procurement asks to get to internal approval.

Short version: we need a temporary carve-out to the standard 99.95% uptime floor for the first 90 days of our go-live window (expected start 2028-09-01). During that period our traffic will ramp >3x and we have hard downstream SLAs we need to protect.

What we're proposing: an interim uptime target of 99.5% for months 1–3 with a capped monthly service credit that scales by severity (we suggested a fixed pool of $5k/month or equivalent credit against usage, whichever is higher), and a clear milestone-based rollback to the standard 99.95% after month 3.

I've attached our request packet (BL_Service_SLA_Requested_Exceptions_v1.pdf) with the expected ramp curve and a short mutual action plan. Can your team confirm whether Redwood is comfortable with a temporary availability entitlement and the proposed credit cap? If not, what's the closest commercial compromise you can offer?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-minute call next week to align.

Jake Turner
Head of Platform Ops, BrightLoop
phone: +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: BL_Service_SLA_Requested_Exceptions_v1.pdf (pdf, 78KB)

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Jake Turner <jake.turner@brightloop.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary uptime floor adjustment + monthly remedy proposal

Jake — appreciate the clear ask and the ramp details. Quick responses to the two main points below.

1) Temporary uptime floor: Redwood can consider a 90-day provisional floor at 99.5% on a case-by-case basis for new, high-throughput customers. We usually require a combination of (a) a dedicated burst allocation, or (b) an initial dedicated capacity commit to avoid noisy-neighbor impacts. Please confirm which route BrightLoop prefers.

2) Monthly credit cap: we can agree to a capped remedy but suggest structuring it as a two-part pool: a fixed monthly credit (we propose $3k/month) plus an additional operational remediation allowance that can be drawn down if there is a platform fault clearly attributable to Redwood (with documented incident review). The goal is to protect both parties and avoid outsized refunds that would constrain capacity provisioning.

I've looped in Laura for contract/terms and Ben for pricing to give quick feedback and attach a redline with our proposed language. If that sounds reasonable, let's run a 30-minute call Thursday to align on the dedicated capacity approach and sign off on the milestones that restore the 99.95% baseline.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachment: redlined-sla-markus-20280705.pdf (redline, 12 pages)

Thanks — looped in a few contract points below we should clarify in the redline. Keeping it tight will help procurement:

• Definition of measurement window — agree on rolling calendar month and the metrics (regional availability vs global). BrightLoop’s attachment shows EU/US split; propose remedy based on the region where traffic originates.

• Triggering incidents vs scheduled maintenance — any scheduled maintenance that was communicated >72 hours in advance should be carved out; we should also define emergency maintenance thresholds.

• Milestone rollback — we need explicit, objective milestones (traffic thresholds and error-rate targets) that Timber (ops) will validate before the baseline reverts to 99.95%. Suggest a short verification window of 14 days after milestones are met.

I made inline comments in redlined-sla-markus-20280705.pdf. Ben — can you confirm the pricing carve (fixed credit + remediation allowance) is feasible within the current term sheet for BL-5421?

Laura Bennett
Staff Counsel, Redwood Inference

Jake — thanks for the packet, confirmed we can accommodate a two-part cap: $3,000/month fixed credit plus a $7,000 remediation allowance that is only payable following an incident review where Redwood is determined to be the primary cause. A few operational clarifications below that will determine how we size dedicated capacity: 

1) We require an initial 3-month committed dedicated burst pool sized at 250 GPU-hours/day during PST peak windows OR an equivalent reserved capacity commit on a monthly cadence. This ensures we can keep tail latency and K/V cache performance stable during ramp.

2) If BrightLoop opts for reserved capacity (preferred), we'll offer a 10% discount on the first three months of committed capacity in exchange for committing to the 3-month window.

3) The remediation allowance is only drawdownable after a post-incident RCA and joint determination. We will make incident timelines explicit in the doc (incident opened, RCA complete within 10 business days).

If that structure works, I can put together a short amendment that we can route for signature. I'm available Thursday 10–11am PT for a call.

Ben Carter
Lead Pricing Manager, Redwood Inference
